notes: Home is rebuilt against the Ford SYNC screen you sent. A vehicle column down the left: big speed, a Ford Ranger drawn from behind with its tail lights lit, reverse lamps that come on with the gear, indicators that blink, and the sixteen parking sensors arranged around it. Under that, two cards and a music player. The big right side is now swipeable pages - one app per page, huge and easy to hit, tap to open fullscreen, swipe for the next, and the last page is the grid of everything installed. Long-press any app to pin or unpin it from the pages. Flat bar along the bottom, no labels-only clutter, with battery voltage on the right. Being straight about the parts of your mockup that are not there: tyre pressures, engine temperature, PRND gear, outside temperature and the entire climate bar are all readings this van returns -1 for, or that do not exist in the CAN interface at all. Rather than draw dead tiles, those slots carry what is real - parking state and battery plus steering. And Android will not let one app draw another inside itself, so Waze is a big bold tile that opens fullscreen rather than a live map panel. The frosted glass and blurred wallpaper are gone for flat dark panels, which is both closer to the reference and one less full-screen blur for the chip to do. Theme now defaults to Midnight. Media panel reads whatever is actually playing and gives you real play, pause and skip - if nothing is playing, or notification access is off, it says so and offers the fix instead of sitting blank. Overlays untouched, as asked - the dock button now opens their menu instead of toggling them by accident.
